summary: The Iraqi Ministry of Justice directly lists a Directorate of Real Estate Registration in Al Qurna, establishing a local cadastral custodian. Official deed/map service routes were reviewed, but current electronic availability is stated to be Baghdad-only and no safe anonymous parcel ID-plus-geometry response was qualified. No sample GeoJSON is retained.
custodian: Iraqi Ministry of Justice, General Directorate of Real Estate Registration; local custodian evidenced as the Directorate of Real Estate Registration in Al Qurna. National Ministry/Ur service pages are not themselves parcel-vector data.
requests: English and Arabic discovery queries and all executed GET routes, outcomes, scope limits, safe-field restrictions, and URLs are recorded in the city record. No login, credentials, CAPTCHA/Cloudflare bypass, private token, unsafe-field request, or TLS exception was used.
safeFieldAllowlist: stable native parcel identifier only if source-proven
full parcel polygon geometry only when safely returned
scopeLimits: The exact WUP point [31.0062665963105, 47.4304356100919] and population 188604 persons are preserved.
The Ministry contact directory is direct evidence of a local registration directorate, but not of anonymous parcel-vector access.
The Ur deed/map service is a transaction workflow and currently states Baghdad-only electronic availability; it was not treated as a public parcel API.
No exact-point hit/miss, map extent miss, timeout, service limitation, or absent geometry response was treated as citywide absence.
No unsafe land-record fields were requested or retained.
Packet completion is not source integration/admission.
uncertainty: The local directorate may have internal or authenticated cadastral maps and records, but those were outside anonymous safe research scope.
No current native parcel identity, geometry schema, CRS, bounded parcel response, or citywide coverage was qualified.
